newsitem.title: UK: Bouquets clutter pavement outside UK Versace store.
newsitem.headline: Bouquets clutter pavement outside UK Versace store.

text.p: Dozens of bouquets cluttered the rain-sodden pavement outside the Versace store in London's Old Bond Street as one of the murdered Italian designer's flagship stores reopened for business on Thursday.

Security guards at the door prevented the merely curious from joining the chic in the elegant emporium which rubs shoulders with jewellers to the queen and other shops dedicated to designer labels in New Bond Street.
"We'll remember you always" read a bouquet in Italian from a Milanese couple visiting London. "Rest in peace. The world has lost an immense talent" read another.
The Versace store was closed on Wednesday as a mark of respect for Gianni Versace, who was murdered in Miami Beach on Tuesday. Some shoppers arrived early to snap up the designer's wares.

"I came yesterday to pay my respects. It was such a shock," said Lisa Zammit from London. "I just think he's brilliant. His clothes are such good quality." By lunchtime, journalists and camera crews outnumbered clients.

Some bought Versace's controversial book Rock and Royalty which caused ructions with Princess Diana, one of his most avid customers, because of its use of photographs of the royal family with those of pop and soccer stars.
"I go to his shop in Milan but the Bond Street store is special because it's so lavish inside - it's like a museum," said Linden Miller from London.
